Leafpile: 2 directions

Make me a font for fall. Pile every letter up from maple, oak, birch and ginkgo leaves in the colors of October. - **What is it for?** A heading at a large size: a harvest fair poster, the title of a fall menu, the letters on a school bulletin board. Not for running text. (I chose this.) - **What should it feel like?** Warm, crisp, a little playful. Like a heap of leaves that a child jumps into. (I chose this.) - **What must it not look like?** A camouflage pattern, a gradient, a font that you must squint at to read, or leaves that look like blobs. (I chose this.) - **Which styles?** One style in each family. `Leafpile` is a color font with four palettes: Maple, Ginkgo, Oak, Late October. `Leafpile Plain` is the same letters in one color. A color font has no variable file. (I chose this.)
